sections.content: You know passive *se* and impersonal *se* from B2 Unit 19, the result with *estar* from B2 Unit 20, and *dicen que* and nouns made from verbs from B2 Unit 21. A news report puts them together so that facts seem to speak for themselves, with no *yo* and often no doer. This lesson adds three ready-made phrases.

sections.title: Three phrases of the news
rows: Se estima que la obra costará dos millones.
It is estimated that the work will cost two million.
Se espera que el ministro llegue mañana.
The minister is expected to arrive tomorrow.
Según fuentes oficiales, el gobierno anunciará nuevas medidas.
According to official sources, the government will announce new measures.

sections.content: *Se estima que* gives a figure or a judgement and takes the indicative. You know *esperar que* from B1 Unit 3: *se espera que* is the same with *se*, so it takes the subjunctive. *Según fuentes oficiales* tells the reader where the information comes from, without naming a person. You know *según* from B1 Unit 13.

items.spanish: Se aprobó la nueva ley ayer.
items.english: The new law was passed yesterday.

items.spanish: Se espera que las cifras mejoren.
items.english: The figures are expected to improve.

items.spanish: Se estima que hay más de mil personas.
items.english: It is estimated that there are more than a thousand people.

sections.content: Compare: *El periodista cree que la crisis termina pronto* (a person) and *Se cree que la crisis termina pronto* (nobody in particular). Choose the impersonal form when the report is about the facts. With a particular person as object, keep the singular verb and the personal *a*, as you learned in B2 Unit 19: *Se busca a los responsables*.
